A2:
**A2 grading note.** Award the point only when the response loops over candidate usernames and, inside the loop body, actually (re)assigns the candidate username string that gets checked for availability — i.e., the concatenated name (requestedName plus the counter, or equivalent) is rebuilt/updated on each pass so that a new potential username is tested each iteration, together with a call to the availability check on a potential username. Errors elsewhere do not matter here: an incorrect call to `isAvailable`, not using `requestedName`, or updating the potential username incorrectly still earn the point so long as the loop body performs some assignment of the candidate name.

Deduct if the loop body never assigns the concatenated name and only changes the counter variable (e.g., the body contains just `suffixNum++;` or `counter++;` while the candidate string was built once before the loop), or if there is no loop at all so the username is fixed before/outside any repetition. Likewise deduct if the availability check is never called, or is called on something that is not a potential username.
A3:
**A3 — Increments a count (in the context of a loop)**

Award the point when the search loop's body actually advances the numeric suffix — i.e., there is a genuine increment of the number variable inside the loop (e.g., `suffixNum++`, `counter++`), so the candidate names demonstrably progress through 1, 2, 3, … for the appended integer — and the name that ends up stored is a verified-available one. That storage requirement is satisfied in either of two shapes: the instance variable is assigned after the loop exits, so whatever name is stored is the one that passed `isAvailable`; or the assignment to `username`/`this.username` occurs inside the loop but is reachable only on the branch where `isAvailable(nameToCheck)` returned true and is immediately followed by `break`/`return`. In both shapes the stored name is one that passed the availability check, and the point stands (the response may still earn it even if the count is never used as part of a possible username or is never initialized).

Deduct when the loop body never changes the number — no increment of the numeric suffix inside the loop, so the same candidate number would be retried indefinitely — or when the in-loop assignment is not guarded by a successful check, i.e., `username`/`this.username` is set to a name that just failed `isAvailable` (assignment on the failing branch, or unconditionally in the loop body without a passing check and immediate `break`/`return`).
A4:
**A4 grading note.** Award the point when the response's algorithm actually consults availability before committing a value to `username` and shows a loop that is visibly trying new names. Concretely: the response must test availability with `isAvailable` (or the equivalent check) and set `username` on the basis of that test; if the numbered form `requestedName + number` is used, the candidate string itself must be (re)assigned inside the loop body, so each pass is offering a new name to the check, and the suffix/counter variable must be declared and initialized *before* the loop so it is at least capable of carrying state across iterations.

Deduct if `username` is set directly from `requestedName` with no `isAvailable` call at all, so availability is never consulted before the value is stored. Also deduct if the loop body merely bumps the counter while the assigned candidate string is left stale (never re-built inside the loop), or if the suffix/counter is declared and initialized inside the loop body so it is re-initialized every iteration.

Do not deduct merely because the counter never changes value, provided the candidate string is reassigned inside the loop body; the visible attempt at new names is sufficient there. Likewise, a counter declared and initialized before the loop satisfies the scope requirement on its own, regardless of how it is later used.
